newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - May 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - May 15.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The final of rugby league's Super League Tri-Series will be between New South Wales and Queensland after New South Wales defeated New Zealand in a controversial game in Canberra last night. NSW won 20-15 after a late try, which could have won the game for NZ, was disallowed by referee Steve Clark. Page 36.

Despite three Australian Football League field umpires considering the incident not reportable, the Western Bulldogs' Chris Grant has been cited on video evidence. Grant was suspended for one week after AFL football operations manager Ian Collins charged Grant with striking. Collins said he will continue to exercise his right to report players, and makes no apologies for reporting Grant. Page 36.

The Victorian Supreme Court is hearing the case of Carlton Australian Football League player Greg Williams, who is seeking a permanent injunction to overrule a penalty by the AFL Tribunal. The AFL argued yesterday Williams' nine-match suspension should rmain, because at no times were his actions accidental. Page 34.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

An Australian jockey was interviewed at Warwick Farm races this week by Hong Kong's Independent Commission Against Corruption. The jockey investigated is believed to be Darren Beadman, but this claim was not confirmed by Australian Jockey Club chief stewrd Ray Murrihy. Page 50.

The Australian women's basketball team play the second match of five against the Russian national team in Sydney tonight. The Russians won the first game 75-70 on Tuesday, but the Australians are confident of levelling the series. Page 48.

The soccer Superstars series later this month will prove a good opportunity for young coaches, with up to three being chosen to gain international experience. The series will be a final selection trial for the World Cup preliminary rounds next month. Page 47.
THE AGE

Australian pace bowlers Glenn McGrath and Jason Gillespie are looking forward to the upcoming cricket Ashes series against England, despite a lack of experience in the country. The Australian team arrived in England this week to complete an extended dometic and international season. Page B8.

The upcoming men's basketball series against Croatia is in doubt after Australian players discovered they were uninsured. Of the top men's side, only Shane Heal is insured, and the other players are considering withdrawal as they would not be fully coverd against injury at practice or during the series. Page B6.

Following an eventful Prime Minister's Cup horse race at the Gold Coast yesterday, top mare French Resort, a second favourite for the Brisbane Cup on June 9, has her immediate future in doubt. The mare dumped jockey Damien Oliver and bolted before yesteray's race, which was eventually won by Starmaker. Page B6.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian Football League chief executive Wayne Jackson has admitted he is nervous about the future of state representative football. Jackson could not guarantee the origin concept would survive but is optimistic about this year's season. Page 88.

Australian basketballer Mark Bradtke has pledged his loyalty to his club side the Melbourne Tigers and not the Olympic national team. Bradtke has not yet decided whether he will continue playing until the Sydney Olympics in 2000, and says he has possiblyachieved everything he can at an international level. Page 82.

Sydney United soccer coach Branko Culina believes the winner of this weekend's preliminary final between Sydney United and South Melbourne will win the final of the Ericsson Cup. Culina said the only remaining opponent, the Brisbane Strikers, were not in the same class as his side or South Melbourne. Page 80.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Steve Small has been appointed coach of the New South Wales cricket team, replacing Geoff Lawson, who was sacked after two reasonably poor years. Other candidates who were not chosen included Len Pascoe, Dave Gilbert and Ashley Mallett. Page 82.

Rugby union centre Richard Tombs fears he will not play for New South Wales again while Matt Williams remains coach. Tombs did not make a 23-man squad for this week's game against Auckland after being dropped following the Blues' big loss to Canberra. Page 80.

Rugby league player Julian O'Neill, recently sacked by the Perth Reds Super League club, is still looking for a new club after Manly ended negotiations with him yesterday. Former Australian Rugby League chairman, and current Manly employee, Ken Arthurson has denied any involvement in the non-selection of O'Neill. Page 79.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
